specs.v: Holds moisture for a long time

description.html: Sphagnum peat comes from peat moss and is one of the substrates that hold moisture the longest. That is why it is used in terrariums for tropical species, where it helps keep humidity from dropping quickly between mistings. It is naturally acidic and has a fine, loose texture.

It is usually not used on its own but mixed with coconut coir: the mix is looser, holds moisture better and compacts less. Adjust the ratio to the species: the more humidity the animal needs, the more sphagnum you add. It suits crested geckos, day geckos, chameleons, frogs and tropical snakes, and it is also a good base for plants in a vivarium. It is not suitable for desert species, which need a dry substrate.

items: Moisten the peat before putting it in the terrarium so it is damp but not wet.
For a humid hide, put a layer of moist peat in a closed box with an entrance; this helps leopard geckos and other species when shedding.
Remove droppings and food leftovers regularly, and replace the substrate when it starts to compact or mold appears.

description.html: The 5-liter pack is enough for a small terrarium, a humid hide or topping up existing substrate. See also our handmade custom terrariums.
